subject: NebulaX-small timeout spike — impact update & mitigation actions
messages:

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-14T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: NebulaX-small: early notice — elevated timeouts this morning

Hi Liam / Angular Health ops,

Wanted to let you know we're actively investigating an uptick in 5xx/timeouts (524-style gateway timeouts and internal request timeouts) affecting requests routed to NebulaX-small starting ~07:50 PDT. Some of your requests hit the affected pool; our monitoring shows a concentrated window and a higher median latency for small-context runs.

Immediate actions we've taken:
- Routing policy updated to divert new NebulaX-small requests to NebulaX-medium where compatible (reduces risk while we triage).
- Increased autoscale headroom on the small pool and enabled conservative request queuing to avoid hard failures.
- Engineering (Dev, Markus) are collecting CPU profiles and kernel logs — we'll share anything that helps with correlation.

Ask from you: if you have a handful of affected trace IDs or example request timestamps, please send them over (even 6–8 examples helps).

ETA: We expect an initial update within 2 hours and a further recovery note once we've validated mitigation. Sorry for the disruption — we're prioritizing stabilization and will follow up with a concrete root cause and next steps.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai

Date: 2027-09-14T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NebulaX-small: early notice — elevated timeouts this morning

Jordan / team — quick triage notes from infra:

What we see:
- Spike in system CPU soft-locks and unusually long syscalls on 3 out of 6 nodes in the NebulaX-small GPU pool starting 07:45 PDT.
- Kernel-level GC + a newly deployed network driver (rollout at 07:30) correlate with increased kernel stalls causing stall durations of 200–800ms. With tight per-request timeouts in the small pool, these stalls manifest as 524/timeouts.
- KV cache eviction rate rose by ~18% after the rollout, increasing recompute caused by cache misses.

Immediate recommended actions (we're executing now):
1) Roll back the 07:30 network driver change on the three impacted nodes (IN PROGRESS).
2) Temporarily widen request timeout on NebulaX-small by +300ms to reduce surface area for partial stalls.
3) Adjust routing to continue favoring NebulaX-medium for latency-sensitive endpoints until postmortem.

I've attached CPU profiles and a short runbook with rollback steps (mitigation_runbook.md). We'll surface the minimal repro traces and link the RW Jira (RW-9876).

Dev
Senior Infrastructure Engineer

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@angularhealth.com>, Support Team <ops@angularhealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-14T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Update: rollback complete, initial recovery observed

Hi Liam — quick update following our mitigation work.

What we did:
- Rolled back the network driver change on the three impacted NebulaX-small nodes at 10:22 PDT.
- Increased small-pool request timeout and continued to route new requests to NebulaX-medium where feasible.

Early results:
- Timeouts attributed to the spike dropped ~60% in the first 30 minutes post-rollback. Error rate for NebulaX-small requests decreased from 3.4% -> 1.2% (still above baseline).
- We continue to monitor and are running an automated smoke test with your representative workloads this hour.

Next steps:
- Engineering will continue sampling and will produce a short postmortem draft by EOD tomorrow with root cause, timeline, and remediation plan.
- If Angular Health would like, we can run a focused acceptance test for your critical endpoints once we confirm steady-state. Tell us preferred window and we'll coordinate.

Thanks again for the quick trace IDs you sent — they helped pinpoint the affected nodes. We'll share the postmortem link when ready.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: NebulaX-small incident: follow-up & postmortem timeline

Hi Liam / Angular Health team,

Wanted to share the next steps following yesterday's incident and confirm our commitments:

1) Postmortem: Draft complete and under review. We'll publish the postmortem (root cause, timeline, mitigation, long-term fixes) to the shared drive and Jira RW-9876 by 2027-09-16 12:00 PDT. Link will be provided.

2) Long-term remediation: engineering proposes a phased plan — (a) tighten rollout gating for kernel/driver changes with canary thresholds, (b) add automatic cross-pool fallback routing at the edge, (c) enhance KV-cache telemetry. Detailed tasks and owners will be in the postmortem.

3) Operational offer: Because this caused customer-visible errors, we'd like to offer a one-time service credit for impacted usage in the incident window; Jordan will coordinate the exact amount with your procurement/finance contact if you accept.

4) Acceptance testing: If Angular Health wants a dedicated acceptance window, we can run it during off-peak hours on 2027-09-17 (we recommend 02:00–04:00 PDT). Let us know and Jordan will schedule.

Apologies again for the disruption. We appreciate the quick collaboration and the logs you provided — that sped up the rollback.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
